source.source_direct_statement: Only when the E2/M1 admixture is known can a definite value for an E0/E2 admixture be extracted.
source.source_boundary: The specified passages do not explicitly discuss t=0, alpha_K(E2)=0, or the 2+->2+ pure-M1/pure-E2 singular parameterization boundaries. Those results below are our analytic reconstruction. The p.123 0+->0+ E0-only remark concerns a distinct case/reference transition.

scope_and_assumptions.synthetic_transition: 2+ -> 2+; no nuclide, Z, energy, atomic coefficients, or measured ICC assigned
scope_and_assumptions.extra_gamma_truncation: retain M1/E2 only; omit the allowed M3/E4 amplitudes explicitly
scope_and_assumptions.penetration: ignored for this derivation; Eq.4.1 includes alpha_K(M1,lambda_pen)
scope_and_assumptions.shell: K-shell only; no assertion about total-shell conversion or pair rates
scope_and_assumptions.normalization_domain: alpha_K(E2)>0; a>0,r>0; finite t>0 requires both retained gamma rates positive
scope_and_assumptions.measurement_conditions: r would require correctly calibrated electron/gamma rates and the correct transition assignment; none are supplied here
scope_and_assumptions.units: T_gamma and T_K are rates in s^-1; Gamma_gamma=hbar*T_gamma has energy units. a,r,t,z,y and every ICC are dimensionless.

definitions.z: q_K^2=T_K(E0)/[alpha_K(E2)*T_gamma(E2)] >= 0; requires nonzero E2 gamma rate
definitions.y: t*z=T_K(E0)/[alpha_K(E2)*T_gamma(M1)] >= 0; requires nonzero M1 gamma rate

boundaries.a_equal_one: r=1+t*z/(1+t)>=1. For r=1, z=0 and t arbitrary; for r>1, z=(r-1)*(1+1/t)>0; r<1 is infeasible.
boundaries.r_equal_one: finite t>0 requires a<=1 and z=(1-a)/t. If a>1 no finite solution; pure-E2 z=0 is a separate endpoint.
boundaries.t_zero_finite_z_formal_extension: r=a, but z uses a zero E2-rate denominator. Keeping z finite as t->0 forces y=t*z->0 and excludes finite E0 only along that path.
boundaries.pure_M1_with_possible_E0: use y: t=0 gives r=a+y with y=r-a>=0; z is undefined. Pure M1 gamma plus E0 electrons is allowed.
boundaries.fixed_z_vs_fixed_y_path: t->0 at fixed finite z gives r->a. At fixed finite y, z=y/t may diverge and r->a+y. These are distinct paths.
boundaries.pure_E2_with_possible_E0: T_gamma(M1)=0 makes t and y singular. Reference the nonzero E2 rate directly: r=1+z>=1.
boundaries.finite_z_t_infinity_identity: r-(1+z)=[a-(1+z)]/(1+t), so t->infinity at fixed finite z gives r->1+z.
boundaries.closed_K_shell: if alpha_K(E2)=0, a,r,z and these normalized bounds are undefined; this does not exclude other-shell E0 or pair channels
boundaries.both_retained_gamma_rates_zero: under the M1/E2 truncation, electron/gamma ICC has zero gamma denominator and is undefined; the omitted allowed gamma components must not be silently assumed absent in the full physical candidate set

ordinary_two_gamma_convex_combination.normalized_range: min(a,1)<=r<=max(a,1); strictly inside at finite t>0 if a!=1
ordinary_two_gamma_convex_combination.ordinary_inverse: if z=0 and a!=1 and r is strictly between a and 1, t=(a-r)/(r-1)>0. If a=r=1, all t have the same ICC.
ordinary_two_gamma_convex_combination.upper_outlier: r>max(a,1) rejects ordinary z=0; positive E0 can fit within the restricted model but is not uniquely demonstrated
ordinary_two_gamma_convex_combination.lower_outlier: r<min(a,1) is impossible even after adding nonnegative E0 in this no-penetration two-gamma model; E0 only raises the ICC
competing_hypotheses: M1 penetration changes the conversion response; p.169 explicitly discusses enhanced electron conversion without enhanced gamma emission

ordinary_two_gamma_convex_combination.inference_boundary: An ICC outside the ordinary two-component hull rejects that assumption package; it alone does not independently prove E0.

identifiability.additional_inputs: an independently constrained radiative mixing magnitude can fix z within the stated source/response model; sign needs interference-sensitive information and a convention map
